A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, experimental results, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including the substantially revised theoretical construction.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figure 2 report original training and test accuracies on edit distance for Looped Transformers with and without timestep encoding.

after.justification: Section 5, Tables 1–3, and Appendix C report original dynamic programming, in-context learning, and language modeling experiments.

M1.justification: The practical timestep-encoding architecture in Section 4.2 is retained. However, the theoretical construction changes extended sequence IDs from 2s(z)-z_N to 2s(Z)-Z_{d,N}. Corollary A.6 consequently introduces an additional coordinate input and a five-coordinate rather than four-coordinate contextual-mapping block.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates only edit distance. V3 retains that task and adds subset sum, knapsack, longest common subsequence, synthetic decision-tree in-context learning, and WikiText-103 language modeling, substantially broadening task and domain coverage.

E2.justification: V1 compares Looped Transformers with and without timestep encoding. V3 adds a 12-layer standard Transformer to the retained edit-distance comparison and includes this comparator in the other reported tasks, materially expanding evaluation beyond the timestep-encoding comparison.

E3.justification: V3 adds five-loop evaluation and task-dependent loop sweeps stopped when accuracy exceeds 90% or saturates. New experiments introduce curriculum training and MSE evaluation for in-context learning, plus wide-block, approximately parameter-matched language-model comparisons at one, three, and six loops using perplexity.

E4.justification: The loop-count sensitivity analysis gains a five-loop edit-distance condition and comparisons distinguishing DP tasks that saturate early from those benefiting from many loops. The training-versus-test edit-distance analysis already appears in v1 Figure 2 and is retained in v3 Appendix C.2 as Figure 5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed information, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V3 continues reporting point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial results in Tables 1–3. Newly reported decision-tree MSE is 1.70e-03 with timestep encoding versus 1.43e-02 for the plain Looped Transformer at 12 loops. On WikiText-103, six-loop test perplexity is 22.42 versus 28.16, while the standard Transformer achieves 19.6. These are new comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.7 changes the delta exponent from -(N+1)d-1 to -1/((N+1)d+1), materially revising the stated rate. Appendix A revises extended-ID definitions, carry/interpolation reasoning, and network consolidation; Lemma 4.1 removes the positive-output assumption. The revised Corollary A.6 nevertheless contains incompatible four- and five-dimensional expressions.

C1.justification: The abstract retains the central claims about approximation rates, loop-specific limitations, and timestep encoding. V3's conclusion adds the empirical contribution that Looped Transformers can solve certain DP tasks that standard Transformers struggle with, extending the contribution beyond v1's edit-distance demonstration.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive distinctions between approximation and generalization, interpreting correlated training/test accuracy as evidence about approximation capacity while attributing standard-Transformer DP limitations to generalization. It discusses language-model test underperformance and explicitly acknowledges unknown approximation-bound tightness and an unexplained mechanism behind DP gains, replacing v1's more general future-work discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix C expands from edit-distance generation into task-specific sampling instructions, examples, decision-tree construction and curriculum details, and language-model tokenization, optimizer, training-budget, context-length, and gradient-accumulation settings. V3 also newly documents learning-rate decay and warm-up for the retained DP setup; this disclosure does not establish that the earlier experiment used a different schedule.

R1.justification: V3 adds related work on parameter sharing and generalization, including Takase and Kiyono, Bae, and Fan; it also connects scaling to Ha's HyperNetworks and expands in-context-learning references. The central positioning as an initial function-approximation analysis of Looped Transformers remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 extensively edits the introduction and theoretical explanations, reorganizes Section 4's motivation, and restructures Section 5 from setup/results into separate experimental questions. It also rewrites the conclusion and reorganizes Appendix A's construction and Appendix C into task-specific subsections, substantially changing the narrative and explanatory structure.

P2.justification: V3 adds a timestep-encoding architecture diagram and three main-text result tables. It moves the original edit-distance plots into Appendix C as Figure 5 and no longer includes v1's separate contextual-ID illustration. These changes substantially reorganize the visual presentation while retaining the proof-overview and quantization illustrations.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the empirical evidence more informative through standard-Transformer controls and evaluations revealing both benefits and limitations, compared with v1's sole edit-distance study. Fuller protocols and explicit uncertainty about bound tightness also improve assessability. However, despite correcting the printed rate exponent, the revised Corollary A.6 retains incompatible matrices in its five-coordinate construction. The empirical and documentation gains support a limited net improvement, with theoretical reliability still unresolved.
